facts.fact: She read the first half of the words over the undercroft's inner door aloud, straight off, and stopped.
facts.evidence: She read it straight off, her lips going along it in the right order.

facts.fact: She counted the undercroft stair the same down and up, and called it a clean page.
facts.evidence: Down and up, both columns, same number. Technically that's a clean page.

facts.fact: She held the lamp for the Captain at the painted wall and did not read the strokes there.
facts.evidence: Wren held the lamp for him the whole time and did not read it

facts.fact: She wrote nothing in her ledger for what was over the door.
facts.evidence: Then she shut the ledger on it

people.did: Counted him down and up; put the words over the inner door into plain speech and told Wren she would not hear them in the hall; walked the dark of the hall without a lamp; made him look at the frost, and kept him from the far end tonight.
people.now: At the head of the undercroft stair with the others, having brought him up at her count.

facts.fact: She put the words over the inner door into plain speech.
facts.evidence: She said it flat, to the lintel

facts.fact: She told Wren she will not hear those words in the hall.
facts.evidence: You'll not hear it in the hall.

facts.fact: She walked the undercroft hall in the dark without a lamp.
facts.evidence: She went round a fallen block of stone without looking down at it

facts.fact: She held him to his word: look, then come up.
facts.evidence: You said you'd look, then come up. You've looked.

people.did: Had himself carried from the Grey Cot to the head of the undercroft stair, and told the Captain down it to look at the wall and not the floor.
people.now: Sitting on the floor at the head of the undercroft stair, his back to the doorframe and his one foot against the linen press.

facts.fact: He told the Captain on the stair to look at the wall, not the floor.
facts.evidence: Look at the bloody wall.

people.did: Waited at the head of the undercroft stair and asked only whether the Captain came up on it.
people.now: At the head of the undercroft stair at supper. She has asked nothing of what he saw.

facts.fact: She will hear what he saw below when he knows what it was.
facts.evidence: You'll tell me what you saw when you know what it was.

codex.name: The undercroft hall
codex.text: Thirty-nine steps down from the undercroft door, cut in the rock and worn hollow in the middle: a hall older than the House, low and vaulted, its pillars cut from the living rock. Its walls are painted with a rank of men and women holding a small cloud of pale strokes over their open hands, and one knight kneeling at a black stone with the light running up out of him along a thread into the vault. Over its inner door, in the old hand: *What is given can be taken. What is built is yours.* Beyond the pillars the flags are white with rime, and the rime climbs the far wall (Ch 3 Sc 4).

fired.evidence: Down and up, both columns, same number. Technically that's a clean page.

now.against: About twenty riders under a banner that is not grey are on the Holloway; under the hall, frost climbs the stone toward the row, and he cannot read what is written there.
now.next: The white beyond the pillars is still unwalked.
